Write a map as a folder that opens with no R and no server

Source: R/bundle.R
rr_bundle.Rd

rr_bundle() writes an rr_map() as a folder whose index.html opens in a browser with a double click, on any system, with no R and no server: the page with the map's config, and beside it the layers' tiles and data as script files (tiles/, data/), which a page opened as a file (file://) may load where it may not fetch them. It needs the internet only for the base maps: MapLibre, maplibre-contour, uPlot and pmtiles are in its vendor folder.

Usage

rr_bundle(
  map,
  dir,
  maxzoom = NULL,
  fit = list(probs = c(0.02, 0.98), n = 25, nodata = 0, slope = list(k = 2, p = 0.9, min
    = 0.3, max = 1)),
  grids = list(),
  overwrite = FALSE
)

Arguments

map

An rr_map().

dir

The folder to write. If it already holds a bundle (index.html, tiles/, data/, grids/, time/ or vendor/), overwrite replaces those and leaves the rest of the folder as it is.

maxzoom

The deepest zoom of the tiles written (dem, contour and vector layers), at most each layer's own; NULL for each layer's own, 14 for a vector layer with none, as the page has it. Past it the map draws that zoom's tiles larger. A lower zoom writes fewer and lighter tiles: dansk's 395,558 points as tiles to zoom 14 are 4,292 tiles and 90 MB, to zoom 12 751 and 53 MB, to zoom 10 160 and 23 MB.

fit

A view's fit in the browser: probs, the percentiles (0-1) of the floor and the cap, with n quantiles from one to the other (for colours in equal shares and contour levels); nodata, an elevation that means no value (NULL for none); slope, a shading's intensity: k over the p percentile of the slope in degrees, kept between min and max. Any left out keeps its default: those of a depth map whose tiles hold 0 on land.

grids

A grid layer's rows for the browser, by the layer's id, each a list of:

  • rows: a data frame or a lazy table (dplyr::tbl() on DuckDB), a row for each cell and combination of the filters' values, with the cell's south-west corner as whole numbers x and y of unit degrees;

  • unit: the degrees of one step of x and y;

  • levels: the cell sizes written, in steps of unit, rising, each a multiple of the rows' own cell;

  • columns: a named character vector, a filter's id to the column it selects on (a range filter's column holds the values its two parameters bound);

  • sums: the columns added up within a cell;

  • fields: a named list, each of the tile's fields a sum's column, or c(<column>, "km2") for that sum per square kilometre of the cell;

  • x, y: the corner's columns, "x" and "y" unless given;

  • px: the filter that scales the cells to that many screen pixels, if any.

overwrite

Whether to replace a bundle already in dir.

Value

dir, invisibly, with the number of tiles written (tiles) and the bundle's size in bytes (bytes) as attributes.

Details

A layer's tiles are one file, a PMTiles archive (version 3) in a script, tiles/<layer>.pmtiles.js, however many tiles it holds, so a bundle is a few files to copy, zip or share. Opened from its folder, the page reads an archive whole on the layer's first need and keeps it, so its memory grows with the tiles' size: for 90-141 MB of tiles, a settled screen 1-2 s later and 300-650 MB more of Chrome's memory than a file a tile took. Put on a web host (http or https), the page reads only what the view needs, by range requests into the same file, as fast and as light as a file a tile; a host that answers no range sends it whole.

What a bundle carries:

  • a geojson layer, its data;

  • a dem or contour layer, its tiles from its minzoom to its maxzoom inside its bounds, written once for the layers that read one file (the source of rr_tiles_dem() and rr_tiles_mbtiles()). Past the deepest zoom written, the map draws that zoom's tiles larger. A view's fit (a colour's, the contours' or a shading's fit) is made in the browser from the layer's tiles in view, by the rules in fit, not by the layer's R function, which needs a server;

  • a vector layer from rr_tiles_table() or a layer function (rr_point() and the others), the tiles that hold a feature, to the deepest zoom written, and the rows a click shows;

  • a time panel (rr_time()), each vessel's spans, the whole and each month, a file each (time/);

  • a grid layer named in grids, its rows: summed by cell at a few cell sizes and written in blocks of cells (grids/), from which the page makes each tile, its filters applied and its cells summed in the browser, with the fields its server would send. Its cells hold one to two screen pixels (the filter px times that), from the cell sizes written. A filter the rows have no column for is left out, with a message.

Another vector layer, or a grid layer not in grids, is left out, with a message: their tiles are made by a server.

See also

rr_serve(), which serves the map from this R session instead.

Examples

places <- sf::st_as_sf(
  data.frame(name = c("Skagen", "Hirtshals"), lon = c(10.59, 9.96), lat = c(57.72, 57.59)),
  coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326
)
layer <- rr_layer(
  "places", "geojson", label = "Places", data = places,
  style = list(list(id = "places-dot", type = "circle", paint = list("circle-color" = "#d9822b"))),
  popup = list(click = "places-dot", title = "name")
)
m <- rr_map(rr_section("ref", "Reference", list(layer)),
            title = "Two harbours", view = list(center = c(10.3, 57.6), zoom = 8))
d <- rr_bundle(m, file.path(tempdir(), "two_harbours"), overwrite = TRUE)
list.files(d, recursive = TRUE)
#>  [1] "data/places.js"                      "index.html"                         
#>  [3] "vendor/LICENSE-maplibre-contour.txt" "vendor/LICENSE-maplibre-gl.txt"     
#>  [5] "vendor/LICENSE-pmtiles.txt"          "vendor/LICENSE-uplot.txt"           
#>  [7] "vendor/maplibre-contour.min.js"      "vendor/maplibre-gl.css"             
#>  [9] "vendor/maplibre-gl.js"               "vendor/pmtiles.js"                  
#> [11] "vendor/uPlot.iife.min.js"            "vendor/uPlot.min.css"               
# utils::browseURL(file.path(d, "index.html"))  # opens it in a browser
